packageRules.description: `n8n-node lint` (@n8n/node-cli) is the lint n8n requires of verified community nodes, and its toolchain is eslint 9: node-cli 0.50.4 depends on eslint 9.29.0 and on eslint-plugin-n8n-nodes-base ^1.16.7, which calls `context.getFilename()` and throws under eslint 10 (https://github.com/beliq-eu/n8n-nodes-beliq/pull/38), and @n8n/eslint-plugin-community-nodes peers eslint 9.29.0. package.json cannot force a newer plugin in, because n8n's scanner rejects an `overrides` field. Lift when @n8n/node-cli depends on eslint 10.

vitest 5 drops Node 20 from its type peer: vitest 4.1.11 peerOptional-requires `@types/node ^20.0.0 || ^22.0.0 || >=24.0.0`, vitest 5.0.0 requires `^22.0.0 || >=24.0.0`. This repo pins `@types/node ^20.14.0` to track its engines floor, so npm cannot resolve and the pull request can never go green. Raising the pin to ^20.19.0 does not help: that satisfies vite 8, which is the conflict npm prints first, but not vitest 5 itself, which is the one that actually blocks. The only pin vitest 5 accepts is ^22 or >=24, and that means raising the engines floor off Node 20 first. Lift this together with engines.node and @types/node, not on its own.

`@types/node` tracks this repo's engines floor, `node >=20.15` in package.json, so a major past 20 would type development against Node APIs the package says it supports running without. Renovate proposed 24 as https://github.com/beliq-eu/n8n-nodes-beliq/pull/23, which is why this rule exists. Same engines-floor fact as the vitest rule above, and lifting the two together with engines.node is the only move that holds: see that rule for what vitest 5 needs. The floor is a per-repo fact, so this stays out of the shared preset.
